Apartments Near Washington Square Mall: A Guide to Living in Tigard, Oregon

If you are searching for apartments near Washington Square Mall, you are searching in Tigard, Oregon. The mall anchors the north side of this southwest Portland suburb, and the Tigard Triangle, where Highway 217 meets Interstate 5, puts shopping, dining, and an easy commute within a few minutes of home. Montage Tigard sits in that pocket at 13155 SW 68th Parkway, a 183 home community with one and two bedroom apartments plus townhomes, and no studios in its published floor plan lineup.

What living near Washington Square Mall is actually like

Washington Square is the center of daily life on this side of Tigard. Washington Square carries more than 170 stores and restaurants, including the largest Nordstrom in Oregon, Macy's, JCPenney, and Dick's Sporting Goods, so most errands, gifts, and weeknight dinners happen within a short drive.

You are not limited to one center, either. Bridgeport Village adds open air shopping and a theater a few minutes south, and downtown Tigard gives you a smaller, walkable local core with independent shops and places to eat. Nike World Headquarters is a short drive north in Beaverton, which matters for a lot of renters who choose this area.

Why renters pick the Tigard Triangle

People choose this pocket of Tigard when they want more room and a shorter commute than the city core without giving up convenience. Highway 217 and Interstate 5 meet right here, so Beaverton, Tualatin, Lake Oswego, and downtown Portland are all reachable without crossing the metro. Nearby neighborhoods vary quite a bit in age, price, and feel, which is worth understanding before you sign. Our guide to the best neighborhoods in Tigard breaks that down.

One and two bedroom apartments, no studios

Floor plan mix is the detail most renters skip when comparing communities near Washington Square, and it is the one that decides whether you actually fit in the home. Some buildings in the area lean heavily on studios and compact one bedrooms.

Montage Tigard publishes one and two bedroom apartments from 686 to 1,338 square feet, plus one, two, and four bedroom townhomes that run as large as 2,281 square feet. There are no studios in the current lineup. You can see the full list on the Montage Tigard floor plans page.

At 183 homes, it is a smaller community than most of what gets built along the 217 corridor, so it trades the scale of a large complex for a quieter, more personal feel.

What rent runs near Washington Square in 2026

As of July 2026, published one bedroom pricing at Montage Tigard starts around $1,850 a month and two bedrooms start around $2,245, with townhome pricing available by request. Pricing moves with availability and lease term, so treat those as a starting point rather than a quote. For a wider view of what a household actually spends here, including utilities, transportation, and groceries, see our Tigard cost of living breakdown.

Inside the homes and around the community

Homes feature quartz counters, walnut style cabinetry, stainless steel appliances, plank flooring, 10 foot ceilings, oversized casement windows, and full size in unit washers and dryers. Most homes include a kitchen island, and first floor homes have private patios.

Around the property there is a pool and spa, a sky lounge, a clubhouse, a fitness center, coworking space, a game room with a golf simulator and arcade games, an on site mini market, private garage parking, EV charging, and controlled access entry. The community is pet friendly with a dog park and a pet spa, no weight limit, and breed restrictions that apply. The full list lives on the amenities page.

If you are still deciding whether this side of the metro fits your weekends, our roundup of things to do in and around Tigard covers the parks, trails, and local spots people actually use.
